Concentration curve from a survey design

Source: R/inequality_extras.R
survey_concentration_curve.Rd

Coordinates of the concentration curve: the cumulative share of the population ranked from poorest to richest (x) against the cumulative share of the health variable (y), both using sampling weights. A curve above the diagonal means the variable is concentrated among poorer people. Tied respondents are grouped into one point, consistent with survey_concentration_index(): the concentration index equals one minus twice the area under the curve.

Usage

survey_concentration_curve(design, outcome, wealth, by = NULL)

Arguments

design

A survey design object (survey or srvyr).

outcome

Unquoted name of the health variable.

wealth

Unquoted name of the ranking variable.

by

Optional character vector of grouping columns; ranks are computed within each group.

Value

A data frame of class surveyncd_curve with any by columns, cum_population and cum_outcome, starting at (0, 0).

Examples

set.seed(1)
df <- data.frame(wealth = rnorm(300), wt = runif(300, 0.5, 2))
df$sick <- rbinom(300, 1, plogis(-1 - 0.6 * df$wealth))
des <- survey::svydesign(ids = ~1, weights = ~wt, data = df)
cc <- survey_concentration_curve(des, sick, wealth)
head(cc)
#>   cum_population cum_outcome
#> 1    0.000000000  0.00000000
#> 2    0.004971117  0.01829262
#> 3    0.007346090  0.02703200
#> 4    0.009712661  0.02703200
#> 5    0.012137815  0.03595604
#> 6    0.015624600  0.04878664
